rationale: A wins because it finds one extra real lens without cooking the facts: "Discord just gave server owners a way to get paid — it won't say how much they'll make" turns the missing earnings data into an honest beat question. B is sharp on proof, especially the app-store stacking issue, but it keeps borrowing unsupplied scaffolding: "Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" and "Discord, Patreon, Twitch, Geneva" are context the update did not give us. Grounded beats glossy; founders do not need a briefing memo dressed up as angles.
gaps_in_A: "Discord's move signals monetization is coming for the whole server, not just the streamer" is a useful thesis, but it stretches one launch into a category claim before the supporting examples exist.
"how this revenue stream fits alongside existing lines (ads, Nitro)" imports revenue lines not supplied in the update.
"it won't say how much they'll make" oversells the data gap. The facts say no creator-earnings data is available because the program is new, not that Discord is withholding it.
"gambling- or loot-box-adjacent" is a speculative diligence question with no factual hook in the update.
gaps_in_B: "Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" and "Discord, Patreon, Twitch, Geneva" are outside facts. Useful after reporting; not clean in a blind grounded angle set.
"Discord opens a paid tier inside community servers built on free membership" relies on "historically been free communities," which the update did not say.
"Discord turns 200M users into a payments business" inflates a platform MAU number into a payments denominator. The uncomfortable question catches this, but the headline still commits the sin.
"journalist-fit-check" is premature as the next step before a beat-matched journalist list exists. Pick the angle, build the list, then fit-check.
